data.title: Kangqiao Service Group Faces Setback as Supreme People’s Court Upholds Loan Judgment
data.description:
Kangqiao Service Group Limited ( (HK:2205) ) has shared an announcement.

Kangqiao Service Group Limited has provided an update on ongoing litigation involving its wholly owned subsidiary, Kangqiao Yueshenghuo Service Group Co., Ltd., relating to irregularities previously discovered in the subsidiary’s bank accounts and associated loan and collateral arrangements. The case centers on a Second Civil Judgment in China, which the company had sought to challenge through a retrial application to the Supreme People’s Court.

The Supreme People’s Court has now dismissed the subsidiary’s retrial application, finding that the evidence submitted on the alleged invalidity of the loan contracts and a promissory letter did not qualify as new evidence sufficient to overturn the original ruling. The court also held that arguments about connected guarantees and listing-rule-related disclosure and approval procedures lacked legal basis, and that the lending bank had carried out appropriate review and was not acting in bad faith.

At the same time, Kangqiao is considering negotiations with the bank to reach a mutually acceptable arrangement over the loan and related collateral to avoid disruption to the subsidiary’s normal operations and mitigate potential impact on business continuity.

The company has urged shareholders and potential investors to exercise caution in trading its shares while the situation develops, underlining that the unresolved litigation and the upheld Second Civil Judgment could have implications for its financial obligations and risk profile. data.title: Shenzhen Investment Restructures Connected Deals via Property Transfer and Ends Development Pact
data.description:
The latest update is out from Shenzhen Investment ( (HK:0604) ).

Shenzhen Investment has arranged for its subsidiary Shenye Wansheng to transfer commercial and office properties to Zhongshan Wanye, settling RMB113.18 million of consideration owed by controlling shareholder Shum Yip Group for a 35.17% equity stake in Shenye Wansheng. The property transfer also offsets an equivalent amount of Shenye Wansheng’s shareholder loan to Shum Yip Group, following a prior RMB30.36 million property-based offset, bringing the aggregated connected transaction to about RMB143.58 million under Hong Kong Listing Rules.

Because these offsetting debt arrangements fall between the 0.1% and 5% percentage ratio thresholds, they are subject to reporting and announcement requirements but exempt from independent shareholders’ approval. In a parallel move, Shenzhen Investment and its partners have terminated a development and construction services agreement with Zhongshan Vanke after Zhongshan Wanye exited its equity holding in Shenye Wansheng, ending those continuing connected transactions and slightly simplifying the company’s connected-party landscape under the Listing Rules.
